beliefs: f collapses every run of adjacent identical characters to a single character [E1, E2, E3]
After collapsing, f removes any character that already appeared earlier in the string, keeping only its first occurrence (case-sensitive: 'E' and 'e' are different) [E1, E2, E5]
f appends 'h' unless the resulting string ends with 'h' or starts with 'h' [E1, E2, E3, E4, E5]
f('hello hello') gives 'helo ' because the second 'helo' is removed as already-seen and the result starts with 'h' so no append [E2]
f('two words') gives 'two rdsh' because the second 'w' and 'o' are removed as already-seen, then 'h' is appended [E1]
f('UPPER lower') keeps both 'e'/'E' and 'r'/'R' because dedup is case-sensitive, so no removal, then 'h' appended [E1]
notes: Discovered that f also removes already-seen characters (keeping first occurrence, case-sensitive), which explains 'two words'->'two rdsh', 'hello hello'->'helo ', and 'a b c'->'a bch'. Combined with collapse-runs and the append-unless-ends/starts-with-h rule, this fits all 5 experiments.
